subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when a disabled provider is selected as the primary or appears in fallbacks?
rationale: Source inspection proves the feature is missing, but adding a config surface and changing provider-routing semantics requires maintainer intent under the repository config-surface policy.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the public flag and implement one shared eligibility helper across config/schema, generation, fallback, catalog/status, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject the new provider flag
options.body: Keep the current operator model where providers are disabled by removing provider blocks or editing fallback/default model references.

options.title: Defer to broader provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until provider enable/disable, setup, auth/status, model picker, and plugin lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the public flag and implement one shared eligibility helper across config/schema, generation, fallback, catalog/status, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the model config, fallback, status, docs, and provider-routing surfaces where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal and prior issue context.
